threads.title: A column is a score, component or cluster label fitted on these same rows, possibly using the outcome
threads.detector: Outcome-blind. Fires on either of two signs. (a) A column that a linear or logit-linear combination of 3 or more other columns reproduces at R2 >= 0.99, with coefficients that match no registered published equation. (b) Model-output names: pred_, prob_, risk, score, fitted, ps_, ipw, PC1..k, cluster. Names only order the question; they never settle it. It must reject a published fixed-coefficient score computed per row (Framingham, CKD-EPI, HEI), so the formula table in clin-derived-clinical-variables serves as its reject list. Dietary specialization: an empirical index (EDIP, EDIH, an RRR pattern score) whose weights were derived in this cohort. A collaborator-supplied propensity score or inverse-probability weight is in scope too.
threads.meaning: score_provenance: a published external equation, an unsupervised transform of all rows, a model fitted on these rows without the outcome, or one fitted with the outcome. Settled by the user or the codebook.

consumers.prediction: Excluded, or rebuilt in-fold. PCs and clusters are recomputed in each training fold.

consumers.inference: A supplied PS or IPW is replaced by one the app fits, so the intervals include the PS step.

threads.failure_prevented: Consequential: HIGH for unblinded diet trials. Family K3 (differential misreporting); the trial sibling of gap G2. Participants in the intervention arm report what they were told to eat, so self-reported effects run larger than biomarker effects. The bias is in the label, so no score can see it. The coverage registry holds ROBINS-I V2 for trials, but RoB 2, the tool for randomized trials, is absent.
threads.magic: Self-reported sodium fell 900 mg more in the intervention arm, but urinary sodium fell by only 300 mg. (Illustrative.)
threads.layout: Angles: the self-reported and objective outcome by arm.
threads.sentence: Because dietary intake was self-reported by unblinded participants, the effect was also estimated on urinary sodium.
sources: Natarajan et al. 2010, Am J Epidemiol 172:819
threads.engine: new.

threads.title: The arm was assigned to schools, clinics or villages, not to people
threads.detector: Outcome-blind. The arm column never varies within a settled grouping (shared-exposure-varies-between-groups at 100% between groups). It reports clusters per arm and the spread of cluster sizes, and checks whether participants enrolled after their cluster was allocated (when dates exist).
threads.meaning: randomization_unit: individual, cluster (which column) or stepped-wedge. Also whether participants were recruited after allocation.

consumers.inference: A mixed model or GEE with a small-sample correction, or a cluster-level analysis when clusters are few.
A predictors-only baseline comparison by arm flags recruitment bias. Individual covariates adjust for it.
The ICC and the design effect are reported, with a sensitivity analysis for recruitment bias.

consumers.decision: CONSORT cluster extension; RoB 2 cluster domain 1b
consumers.inference: Stated.

threads.failure_prevented: Consequential: HIGH. Family S4, with S5. An individual-level analysis of a 12-school trial reports intervals as if 2,400 children had been randomized. Children recruited after allocation can differ by arm. School-based nutrition trials are common, and no thread names cluster randomization.
threads.magic: The arm never varies within a school. Twelve schools were randomized, not 2,400 children, so your effective sample is much closer to 12. (Illustrative.)
threads.layout: Flow: clusters by arm, then participants within them.

Leyrat et al. 2018, Int J Epidemiol 47:321

threads.title: In a long table, a per-person column summarizes all of the person's visits, future ones included
threads.detector: Outcome-blind. A column constant within each unit that equals an aggregate of a time-varying column over all of that unit's rows (row count, max, min, last, any, mean), or that carries summary names (ever_, n_visits, final_, max_, total_). It must reject a baseline value carried forward, which equals the first row's value and is legitimate.

consumers.inference: As a covariate it is post-baseline, so it goes to the K4 card's after-exposure row. Used as the exposure, it creates immortal time (shared-time-zero).

Stated.

threads.failure_prevented: Consequential: HIGH for longitudinal prediction. Family S2. A per-person 'n_visits' or 'max_hba1c' gives every early row the future. Grouped folds do not help, because the leak runs within the unit's own rows. shared-repeats-or-time-points refuses summaries that the app itself builds after the outcome, but not summary columns the collaborator delivered.

threads.title: An identifier is unique only within a site, cycle or file, so two people share one ID
threads.detector: Outcome-blind. An ID repeats across levels of site, cycle or file, and within the ID the time-invariant attributes (sex, birth year) contradict each other, or encounter dates overlap at two sites. threads.detector: Outcome-blind. A text predictor with 3 to 10 levels matching an ordinal vocabulary (education levels; never/former/current; low/medium/high; quintile labels) where alphabetical order differs from the vocabulary's. Mirrors structural.order_question, which today runs for outcomes only.

threads.title: A key confounder is measured so poorly that adjusting for it leaves most of its confounding
threads.detector: Outcome-blind. Applies to a settled confounder (from the K4 card) that is self-reported, a single reading, or coarsened (smoking yes/no with no pack-years), or whose replicate or reference measure shows low reliability. A registry lists confounders known to be noisy in nutrition: physical-activity questionnaires, smoking status, SES proxies.

threads.title: The exposure is assigned from a group or predicted by a model (Berkson-type error), not measured with noise
threads.detector: Outcome-blind. The exposure is constant within a grouping such as household, school menu, area or food-composition value (shared-exposure-varies-between-groups at about 100% between groups). Or it is a model's output: predicted usual intake, an imputed biomarker, an equation estimate, a calibrated FFQ, or names like pred_, est_, usual_.

notes:
I am the completeness critic, picking up after the usage limit. The previous completeness run (agent a8cc519d) failed and left nothing behind. I read the repo only. The one computation was a small pandas read of clinic_visits.csv and clinical_labs/clinical_longitudinal.csv, which supplies the counts marked "Measured".

The single biggest finding is a pipeline loss, not a domain gap.

**1. Nine shared threads never reached the "333".**
- **What happened:** final:shared was handed a truncated merge+gaps_shared catalog that stopped partway through the 95 threads. Its report says threads 87-95 "are gone" and that no copy exists. A copy does exist: in the workflow journal (subagents/workflows/wf_344f7bf3-8ad/journal.jsonl), in the merge+gaps result. I extracted it to scratchpad/crit/merge+gaps_shared.json.
- **Two of the nine were rebuilt under other names:** spatial-neighbors became shared-spatial-dependence, and the dropout half of observation-process became shared-informative-dropout.
- **Seven are substantively missing** (the first seven entries above): score-fitted-on-these-rows, target-population-shift, overfit-calibration-slope, decisions-after-viewing, winner-optimism, rashomon-disagreement and learned-interaction.
- **Why they matter:**
  - They are most of the late-born threads for evaluation × prediction and explanation × prediction.
  - Report §4 currently answers TRIPOD+AI 23a, PROBAST 4.8, KN L1.3 and ROBINS-E D7 with "by construction" or with weaker threads. Each of those items needs one of these seven as its sentence-bearing thread.
  - So the 333 total, the family counts (E2 16, E3 8, S3 8, S7 9), Appendix A and the §4 coverage maps all need updating.
- **What remains of observation-process:** only its visit-intensity reading outside the clinical lens (EMA, panels). I left it as a note rather than a thread.

**2. Concepts dropped between the sweeps and the merge.** I checked every sweep thread id against the finals. These five never landed and have no equivalent: shared-upstream-subset, shared-mismeasured-confounder, shared-many-versions-of-exposure, shared-ordered-text-levels and shared-tail-is-a-population. The first four are in the list above. The fifth is mostly covered by impossible-vs-extreme.

**3. Engine noticings with no thread.** U4 says findings migrate into threads, so any finding without a thread would be orphaned:
- category_variants (ml/import_doctor.py:842);
- positive_class (ml/binary_text.py:289);
- the seal floor (core/seal.py:603-718);
- role:free_text (core/readings.py:1118).

These four are in the list above. The structural ones are covered: empty, footer, header-in-later-row, duplicate and constant columns, unnamed columns and wide repeats. Recommendation: add a census test so that every engine finding id maps to a thread, or is declared silent with a reason. That is the engine-side twin of §3.5.

**4. The coverage registry is narrower than the anchors the catalogs already cite.**
- **What the catalogs cite:** STROBE-ME (16 threads), STREGA (10), MIAME (11), CONSORT (6), AAPOR and CHERRIES (2), and STARD (1).
- **What the registry holds:** PROBAST, ROBINS-E, ROBINS-I V2, KN, TRIPOD+AI and STROBE-nut only.
- **The consequence:** unmapped items in the cited frameworks cannot turn the test red.
- **Frameworks to add:** RoB 2 and CONSORT 2025 with its cluster extension (the app supports trials, and ROBINS-I is the wrong tool for them); TRIPOD-Cluster for multi-site prediction; RECORD for EHR and linkage; STROBE-ME; STREGA and GRIPS; STARD and QUADAS-2 (clin-partial-verification); MIAME, MINSEQE and MSI; STORMS (microbiome); AAPOR.
- **Threads they surfaced:** mapping RoB 2 alone produced shared-outcome-assessed-knowing-the-arm and shared-cluster-randomized.
- **Still open:** the PROBAST+AI item list is unverified, as the report itself says.

**5. Data types missing from the lenses.** Microbiome (genomics-microbiome-composition) and affinity proteomics (metab-affinity-proteomics: Olink NPX or SomaScan). Both are central to current nutrition research. Neither appears in any catalog: "microbio" has 1 incidental hit, and "Olink", "NPX" and "aptamer" have none. A user with these data would pick a lens whose K1 rules are wrong for them.

**6. Nutrition-specific measurement gaps.** These came from looking at lens × stage, not at the frameworks:
- recall day before the draw: correlated error, so regression calibration is invalid;
- spot-urine estimated excretion: the Kawasaki and INTERSALT equations;
- lipid-carried micronutrients: lipid standardization of vitamin E;
- borrowed validity coefficients: regression calibration from external data for FFQ-only studies;
- the Berkson versus classical error structure. All K3 threads assume classical error, so regression calibration would over-correct a group-assigned exposure.

**7. Data-shape gaps.**

| Shape | Status |
|---|---|
| Wide | Covered, except unequal blocks |
| Longitudinal | Missing: delivered unit summaries that span the future; counting-process intervals |
| Multi-site | Missing: IDs unique only within a site; columns missing for whole sites or cycles; cluster randomization |
| Rare outcome | Missing: event-level choice; holdout floor |
| Small n | Missing: holdout floor; winner optimism |
| Rows standing for many | Missing: frequency weights and aggregated rows |

**8. The 17 families are closed over validity, not over obligations.** Disclosure and privacy (shared-identifiable-values-in-the-export) fit no family. So do data-use terms, such as NHANES's requirement to use weights and its restricted linked files. Either add an obligation family, or have the registry state that obligations are outside it.

**Most consequential, if only ten are built next:**
1. score-fitted-on-these-rows
2. overfit-calibration-slope
